title: Quick sort
short: Pick a pivot, put smaller left and bigger right, repeat.
what: Choose one value, the pivot. Move everything smaller than it to its left and everything bigger to its right. The pivot is now in its final place. Do the same to the left part and the right part until every part is tiny.
analogy: Sorting a class by height. Pick one student; everyone shorter stands on their left, everyone taller on their right. That student is now in the right spot, and each side repeats on its own.

frames.say: Repeat on each side: 2, 4, 3 becomes 2, 3, 4 and 9, 8, 7 becomes 7, 8, 9. Sorted, without an extra list.

when: Sort in place with little extra memory
Find the k-th smallest without a full sort (quickselect)
Average speed matters more than the worst case
python:
def quick_sort(a, lo, hi):
    if lo >= hi:
        return
    pivot, i = a[hi], lo
    for j in range(lo, hi):
        if a[j] < pivot:
            a[i], a[j] = a[j], a[i]
            i += 1
    a[i], a[hi] = a[hi], a[i]
    quick_sort(a, lo, i - 1)
    quick_sort(a, i + 1, hi)

nums = [7, 2, 9, 4, 3, 8, 5]
quick_sort(nums, 0, len(nums) - 1)
print(nums)
watch: Always taking the last value as pivot is O(n²) on already sorted input. Pick a random pivot.
It is not stable: equal items can swap order.
For the k-th smallest, recurse into only one side: O(n) on average.
